data.title: Campaign Measures and Adapts to Its Own Reach
data.summary:
The campaign demonstrably adapts to performance — abandoning content that gained no
traction, re-using what did, and shifting platforms as enforcement bites — indicating
active management rather than automated repetition.
data.description:
An operation that measures itself is being run by somebody, and that changes what the
client is dealing with. Automated repetition decays predictably and can be waited out.
Managed campaigns respond to the client's actions, including its defensive ones, and a
response that works once will be adapted against.

The evidence is behavioural: content that fails is dropped quickly, successful framings
recur with variations, and activity migrates ahead of enforcement rather than after it.
Use of link shorteners and tracking parameters is a more direct indicator, since it shows
the operator instrumenting its own delivery.

This finding should shape the recommendations in the rest of the report. Measures that
assume a static adversary will be worked around.
data.recommendation:
* Assume the campaign will adapt to any public response, and sequence the response
  accordingly rather than revealing the full picture at once.
* Avoid publicly describing detection methods; doing so tells a measuring operator what to
  change.
* Track which of the client's actions produce adaptation — it is a reliable signal of what
  the operator cares about.
data.short_recommendation: Assume adaptation; do not publicise detection methods.
